meta.description: Provide current date and time information to requesting services via IBM MQ messaging, acting as a centralised date/time service within the CardDemo credit card management system.
meta.process_description: CODATE01 operates as a CICS-hosted MQ listener service that receives date/time enquiry requests from other system components via an IBM MQ input queue. Upon receiving a request, the program retrieves the current system date and time and returns the formatted response to the caller via a dedicated reply queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE). The program processes messages in a continuous loop until no more messages are available, committing each transaction via CICS SYNCPOINT to ensure message integrity. Any processing errors are routed to a centralised error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) for operational monitoring and fault management.

files.CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE: Output MQ queue where formatted date/time responses are delivered back to requesting services
files.CARD.DEMO.ERROR: Centralised MQ error queue for capturing and routing processing failures and system errors for operational monitoring
files.ACCTDAT: Credit card account data file (referenced in working storage, likely inherited from shared copybooks rather than directly used by this program)

business_rules: Each message retrieved from the input queue must be processed within a CICS SYNCPOINT boundary to guarantee exactly-once delivery and prevent message loss or duplication.
If the MQ input queue, output reply queue, or error queue cannot be opened at startup, the program must terminate immediately rather than process requests with incomplete infrastructure.
All error conditions (queue open failures, CICS retrieve failures) must be reported to the centralised CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue to ensure operational visibility across the CardDemo platform.
The program waits up to 5000 milliseconds (5 seconds) for a new message before concluding that no more messages are available and terminating gracefully.
The reply queue name is hardcoded as CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE, establishing a fixed service contract between this date utility and its consumers.
The program initialises as INITIAL, meaning each CICS invocation starts with a clean working storage state, ensuring no stale date/time data is returned from a previous execution.

variables.description: A named condition that evaluates to true when the input queue contains no further date/time service requests. When true, the program stops polling and ends its processing cycle cleanly.

variables.name: WS-RESP-QUEUE-STS
variables.description: A status flag indicating whether the response queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) was successfully opened at startup. If this remains 'N', the program cannot deliver date/time responses and must terminate immediately per business rules.

variables.name: RESP-QUEUE-OPEN
variables.description: A named condition confirming that the reply queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) is open and ready to receive formatted date/time responses. The program must verify this before attempting to serve any requests.

variables.name: WS-ERR-QUEUE-STS
variables.description: A status flag indicating whether the centralised error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) was successfully opened at startup. If this remains 'N', the program cannot report failures to operations and must terminate immediately, as error visibility is a mandatory business requirement.

variables.name: ERR-QUEUE-OPEN
variables.description: A named condition confirming that the centralised error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) is open and available for fault reporting. Without this, the program cannot fulfil its obligation to provide operational visibility of failures across the CardDemo platform.

variables.name: WS-REPLY-QUEUE-STS
variables.description: A status flag indicating whether the dynamic reply-to queue (specified by the requesting service in the incoming message header) was successfully opened. This ensures the date/time response can be routed back to the correct requester.

variables.name: REPLY-QUEUE-OPEN
variables.description: A named condition confirming that the dynamic reply-to queue from the incoming request header is open and ready. The program uses this to verify it can route the date/time response back to the specific service that made the request.

variables.name: WS-CICS-RESP-CDS
variables.description: A group record holding the CICS response codes returned after each CICS service call (such as retrieving a message or issuing a SYNCPOINT). These codes are examined to detect failures in transaction processing and trigger appropriate error handling.

variables.name: WS-CICS-RESP1-CD
variables.description: The primary CICS response code returned after a CICS command executes. A non-zero value indicates a failure in the CICS transaction environment, such as a problem retrieving a message or committing a SYNCPOINT, which must be routed to the error queue.

variables.name: WS-CICS-RESP2-CD
variables.description: The secondary CICS response code providing additional diagnostic detail when a CICS command fails. Used alongside the primary response code to give operations staff a precise understanding of what went wrong during transaction processing.

variables.name: WS-CICS-RESP1-CD-D
variables.description: A display-formatted copy of the primary CICS response code, used when constructing human-readable error messages to be sent to the centralised error queue or written to operational logs.

variables.name: WS-CICS-RESP2-CD-D
variables.description: A display-formatted copy of the secondary CICS response code, used when constructing human-readable error messages to support operational diagnosis of transaction failures.

variables.name: WS-DATE-TIME
variables.description: A group record holding the current date and time information that is the core output of this service. It contains the raw system timestamp and the formatted date and time values that will be packaged into the response message sent back to requesting services.

variables.name: WS-ABS-TIME
variables.description: The raw absolute system timestamp retrieved from CICS, representing the number of milliseconds since a fixed reference point. This internal value is used as the source from which the human-readable date (MM/DD/YYYY) and time are derived for inclusion in the service response.

variables.name: WS-MMDDYYYY
variables.description: The current system date formatted as MM/DD/YYYY, which is the primary business output of this date service. This formatted date is included in the response message delivered to requesting services via the CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE queue.

variables.name: WS-TIME
variables.description: The current system time formatted for human readability, included alongside the date in the response message. Consuming services can use this to timestamp transactions or audit records with the precise time the date service was called.

variables.name: MQ-QUEUE
variables.description: A working field holding the name of an MQ queue being operated on during processing. Used as a general-purpose queue name holder when opening or interacting with MQ queues as part of the date/time service workflow.

variables.name: MQ-QUEUE-REPLY
variables.description: A working field holding the name of the reply queue to which the formatted date/time response will be sent. This is populated from the incoming request message header to enable dynamic routing of responses back to the correct requesting service.

variables.name: MQ-HCONN
variables.description: The MQ connection handle representing the active session between this program and the MQ queue manager. This handle must be established before any messages can be read from the request queue or written to the reply and error queues.

variables.name: MQ-CONDITION-CODE
variables.description: The completion code returned by MQ after each queue operation (open, get, put). A non-zero value signals a problem with the messaging infrastructure, such as a failure to open a queue or deliver a response, which must be reported to the error queue.

variables.name: MQ-REASON-CODE
variables.description: The detailed reason code returned by MQ explaining why an operation failed or completed with a warning. This code is included in error messages sent to CARD.DEMO.ERROR to help operations staff diagnose messaging infrastructure problems.

variables.name: MQ-HOBJ
variables.description: The MQ object handle for a specific queue that has been opened. This handle is used in subsequent get or put operations to reference the correct queue without re-specifying the queue name each time.

variables.name: MQ-OPTIONS
variables.description: A bitmask of options controlling how an MQ queue operation behaves, such as whether to wait for a message, browse only, or open for exclusive input. These options govern the reliability and behaviour of message retrieval and delivery.

variables.name: MQ-BUFFER-LENGTH
variables.description: The maximum size of the message buffer allocated to receive an incoming date/time service request from the MQ queue. This prevents buffer overflow when reading request messages of varying sizes.

variables.name: MQ-BUFFER
variables.description: The raw message buffer holding the content of a date/time service request retrieved from the input MQ queue. The program reads this buffer to extract the function code and key identifying what the requesting service needs.

variables.name: MQ-DATA-LENGTH
variables.description: The actual length of the message data retrieved from the MQ queue. This tells the program how many bytes of the buffer contain meaningful request content, as opposed to padding, ensuring correct parsing of the incoming service request.

variables.name: MQ-CORRELID
variables.description: The MQ correlation identifier associated with the current message being processed. This ID links the outgoing date/time response to the original request, allowing the requesting service to match the reply to its original query.

variables.name: MQ-MSG-ID
variables.description: The unique message identifier assigned by MQ to each incoming date/time service request. Used for message tracking and deduplication, ensuring that each request is processed exactly once within the CICS SYNCPOINT boundary.

variables.name: MQ-MSG-COUNT
variables.description: A running count of the number of date/time service requests processed during the current execution cycle. This counter provides operational visibility into throughput and can be used for monitoring and audit purposes.

variables.name: SAVE-CORELID
variables.description: A saved copy of the MQ correlation ID from the incoming request message. Preserved before any MQ operations overwrite the working field, so the correct correlation ID can be stamped on the outgoing date/time response to ensure it is matched to the right requester.

variables.name: SAVE-MSGID
variables.description: A saved copy of the unique message ID from the incoming request. Retained so that the response message can reference the original request ID, supporting end-to-end message traceability across the CardDemo platform.

variables.name: SAVE-REPLY2Q
variables.description: The reply-to queue name extracted from the incoming request message header and saved for use when sending the date/time response. This enables dynamic routing so that each requesting service receives its response on its own designated queue, rather than a single fixed destination.

variables.name: MQ-ERR-DISPLAY
variables.description: A structured error message record assembled when an MQ or processing failure occurs. This record is formatted and sent to the centralised CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue so that operations staff have a clear, consistent description of what failed, where, and why.

variables.name: MQ-ERROR-PARA
variables.description: The name of the program paragraph or processing step where the error occurred. Included in the error message to help operations staff pinpoint exactly which part of the date/time service failed.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A spacing separator between fields in the error message record, improving readability of error messages delivered to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue and any operational logs.

variables.name: MQ-APPL-RETURN-MESSAGE
variables.description: A short descriptive text message explaining the nature of the error encountered during date/time service processing. Provides operations staff with a human-readable summary of the failure without needing to decode numeric error codes.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A spacing separator between fields in the error message record, improving readability of error messages delivered to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue and any operational logs.

variables.name: MQ-APPL-CONDITION-CODE
variables.description: The MQ completion code captured at the time of failure, included in the error message sent to CARD.DEMO.ERROR. Allows operations staff and support teams to quickly classify the severity of the messaging failure.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A spacing separator between fields in the error message record, improving readability of error messages delivered to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue and any operational logs.

variables.name: MQ-APPL-REASON-CODE
variables.description: The detailed MQ reason code captured at the time of failure, included in the error message sent to CARD.DEMO.ERROR. Provides the specific technical cause of the messaging failure to support rapid diagnosis and resolution by operations or development teams.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: A spacing separator between fields in the error message record, improving readability of error messages delivered to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue and any operational logs.

variables.name: MQ-APPL-QUEUE-NAME
variables.description: The name of the MQ queue that was being accessed when the error occurred (input, reply, or error queue). Included in the error message to tell operations staff exactly which queue in the CardDemo messaging infrastructure caused the failure.

variables.name: MQ-GET-MESSAGE-OPTIONS
variables.description: A group record containing the options that control how the program retrieves date/time service request messages from the input MQ queue, including settings such as the 5-second wait timeout before concluding no more requests are available.

variables.name: MQ-PUT-MESSAGE-OPTIONS
variables.description: A group record containing the options that control how the program delivers date/time response messages to the reply queue or error messages to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue, governing delivery guarantees and message properties.

variables.name: MQ-MESSAGE-DESCRIPTOR
variables.description: A group record representing the MQ message header (MQMD) attached to each message. Contains metadata such as message ID, correlation ID, and reply-to queue name that the program uses to correctly route date/time responses back to requesting services.

variables.name: MQ-OBJECT-DESCRIPTOR
variables.description: A group record describing the MQ queue object to be opened, including the queue name and queue manager name. Used during startup when opening the input, reply, and error queues to establish the messaging infrastructure required for the date/time service.

variables.name: MQ-CONSTANTS
variables.description: A group record holding standard IBM MQ constant values used throughout the program, such as option flags for queue open modes and message get/put behaviours. These constants ensure the program interacts with MQ in a standardised and reliable way.

variables.name: MQ-GET-QUEUE-MESSAGE
variables.description: A group record representing the structure of a date/time service request message retrieved from the input MQ queue. The program parses this structure to extract the function code and key identifying what the requesting service requires.

variables.name: QUEUE-INFO
variables.description: A group record holding the names of all MQ queues used by the date/time service: the queue manager, the input request queue, the reply queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE), and the error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR). These names define the complete messaging topology of the service.

variables.name: QMGR-NAME
variables.description: The name of the IBM MQ queue manager that hosts all queues used by the date/time service. This identifies the MQ server infrastructure that the program must connect to before it can process any date/time service requests.

variables.name: INPUT-QUEUE-NAME
variables.description: The name of the MQ queue from which incoming date/time service requests are consumed. Other CardDemo services place their requests on this queue, and this program reads from it to provide the current date and time in response.

variables.name: REPLY-QUEUE-NAME
variables.description: The hardcoded name of the MQ reply queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) to which formatted date/time responses are delivered. This fixed queue name establishes the service contract between the date utility and all consuming services in the CardDemo platform.

variables.name: ERROR-QUEUE-NAME
variables.description: The name of the centralised MQ error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) to which all processing failures and infrastructure errors are routed. This ensures that any failure in the date/time service is visible to operations staff monitoring the CardDemo platform.

variables.name: INPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE
variables.description: The MQ object handle for the open input request queue. Once the input queue is successfully opened at startup, this handle is used in all subsequent message retrieval operations to consume incoming date/time service requests.

variables.name: OUTPUT-QUEUE-HANDLE
variables.description: The MQ object handle for the open reply queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE). Used when putting formatted date/time response messages onto the reply queue to be consumed by the requesting service.

variables.name: ERROR-QUEUE-HANDLE
variables.description: The MQ object handle for the open centralised error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR). Used when routing error messages to operations, ensuring that any failure during date/time service processing is captured and visible for monitoring.

variables.name: QMGR-HANDLE-CONN
variables.description: The connection handle representing the active session between this program and the MQ queue manager. All queue open, get, and put operations depend on this handle being valid, making it the foundation of the entire date/time service messaging capability.

variables.name: QUEUE-MESSAGE
variables.description: A general-purpose message buffer used to hold the content of messages being sent to or received from MQ queues during processing. Used for constructing outgoing date/time response messages or error messages before they are put onto the appropriate queue.

variables.name: REQUEST-MESSAGE
variables.description: A preserved copy of the raw incoming date/time service request message retrieved from the input queue. Retaining the original request allows the program to reference the requester's function code and key while constructing the appropriate response.

variables.name: REPLY-MESSAGE
variables.description: Business meaning: The formatted response payload sent back to the requesting service containing the current date and time information. This is the actual message body delivered to the CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE queue, fulfilling the date/time service contract with the consumer.

variables.name: ERROR-MESSAGE
variables.description: Business meaning: The error notification payload routed to the centralised CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue when a processing failure occurs. This message captures fault details to ensure operational teams across the CardDemo platform are alerted to any date/time service failures.

variables.name: REQUEST-MSG-COPY
variables.description: Business meaning: The structured layout of an incoming date/time service request message retrieved from the input MQ queue. It defines how the program interprets the raw message bytes received from a requesting service within the CardDemo system.

variables.name: WS-FUNC
variables.description: Business meaning: The service function code sent by the requesting system, identifying what type of date/time operation is being requested. This allows the date/time service to distinguish between different request types if multiple service variants are supported, acting as the instruction from the consumer to the service.

variables.name: WS-KEY
variables.description: Business meaning: The unique identifier of the requesting entity or transaction, such as an account number or transaction reference, included in the incoming request. This key allows the date/time service to associate the response with the correct business context or originating requester within the CardDemo system.

variables.name: WS-FILLER
variables.description: Business meaning: Reserved padding space within the incoming request message structure to bring the total message length to 1000 bytes. This ensures the request message conforms to the fixed-length MQ message format agreed upon between the date/time service and its consumers, accommodating future extensions to the request payload without breaking the service contract.

variables.name: WS-VARIABLES
variables.description: Business meaning: A collection of general-purpose working variables used internally by the date/time service during processing, including infrastructure identifiers and system response tracking fields needed to manage queue operations and error handling.

variables.name: LIT-ACCTFILENAME
variables.description: Business meaning: The name of the credit card account data file (ACCTDAT) used as a reference identifier within the CardDemo system. Although this date/time service does not directly process account records, this field is likely inherited from shared copybooks common across the CardDemo platform, maintaining consistency with the broader system's file naming conventions.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: Business meaning: The CICS response code returned after each infrastructure operation such as opening an MQ queue or retrieving a message. A non-zero value signals that a system-level failure has occurred, triggering the error handling process and routing a fault notification to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue to alert operations teams.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: Business meaning: The CICS reason code providing additional detail about why a particular infrastructure operation failed, complementing the response code. This granular fault information is included in error messages sent to the CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue, helping operational teams diagnose the specific cause of a date/time service failure.

paragraphs.name: 1000-CONTROL
paragraphs.description: Orchestrates the full lifecycle of the date/time service: initialises the messaging infrastructure, identifies the requesting input queue, and drives the message processing loop until all pending requests have been fulfilled and the service shuts down cleanly.

paragraphs.name: 2300-OPEN-INPUT-QUEUE
paragraphs.description: Establishes the service's connection to the incoming date/time request queue, making it ready to receive and consume service requests from other CardDemo components. If the queue cannot be opened, the program immediately halts to prevent operating with incomplete messaging infrastructure.

paragraphs.name: 2400-OPEN-OUTPUT-QUEUE
paragraphs.description: Establishes the outbound messaging channel to the date/time reply queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE), enabling the service to deliver formatted date/time responses back to requesting systems. If the reply queue cannot be opened, the program halts immediately to prevent processing requests that cannot be fulfilled.

paragraphs.name: 2100-OPEN-ERROR-QUEUE
paragraphs.description: Establishes the connection to the centralised CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue so that any processing failures encountered during the service's operation can be routed to operational monitoring. If this error-reporting channel cannot be opened, the program terminates immediately rather than risk running without fault visibility.

paragraphs.name: 4000-MAIN-PROCESS
paragraphs.description: Anchors each date/time service request within a transaction integrity boundary before retrieving and processing the next incoming message, ensuring that every request is handled exactly once without risk of duplication or message loss.

paragraphs.name: 3000-GET-REQUEST
paragraphs.description: Attempts to retrieve the next pending date/time service request from the input MQ queue, waiting up to 5 seconds for a message to arrive. On success, captures the caller's routing details and triggers response processing; on queue exhaustion, signals orderly shutdown; on failure, escalates the error and terminates.

paragraphs.name: 4000-PROCESS-REQUEST-REPLY
paragraphs.description: Captures the current system date and time, formats them into a human-readable response message, and dispatches the reply back to the requesting service. This is the core fulfilment step of the date/time service contract.

paragraphs.name: 4100-PUT-REPLY
paragraphs.description: Delivers the formatted date/time response back to the requesting service via the designated MQ reply queue, ensuring the reply is correctly correlated to the original request. If the delivery fails, the error is escalated to the centralised error queue and the program terminates to prevent incomplete or undeliverable responses.

paragraphs.name: 9000-ERROR
paragraphs.description: Routes error details to the centralised CARD.DEMO.ERROR queue so that operational teams can monitor and investigate processing failures within the CardDemo date/time service. If the error queue itself cannot accept the message, the program captures the secondary failure and initiates a controlled shutdown.

paragraphs.name: 8000-TERMINATION
paragraphs.description: Performs an orderly shutdown of the date/time service by releasing all MQ queue connections before terminating, ensuring no queue resources are left open and the service exits cleanly after completing its processing cycle.

paragraphs.name: 5000-CLOSE-INPUT-QUEUE
paragraphs.description: Releases the MQ input queue once all date/time service requests have been consumed, ensuring the messaging infrastructure is cleanly disconnected. If the queue cannot be closed properly, the failure is escalated to the centralised error queue and the program terminates to prevent resource leaks.

paragraphs.name: 5100-CLOSE-OUTPUT-QUEUE
paragraphs.description: Releases the reply queue (CARD.DEMO.REPLY.DATE) once all date/time responses have been delivered, ensuring the messaging channel is cleanly shut down. If the queue cannot be closed gracefully, the program escalates to a controlled termination to protect messaging infrastructure integrity.

paragraphs.name: 5200-CLOSE-ERROR-QUEUE
paragraphs.description: Releases the centralised error queue (CARD.DEMO.ERROR) once all processing is complete, ensuring the messaging infrastructure is cleanly shut down. If the queue cannot be closed gracefully, the failure is logged and the program terminates immediately to prevent resource leaks.
